state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs) is under way.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done; Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. `Core\Ldap` owes nothing: `connect` and `open` each have an `about.md`, three examples, an attack, a bench with a recorded figure, and a `covers:` marker on their grant tests in `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs`.

**How those proofs run with no server**, on `Core\Mail::send`'s footing: the root `nvs.toml` has an `[ldap.corp]` block at `ldaps://127.0.0.1:1`, a closed port, and one `[[app]] entry` per proof program granting `ldap.connect = ["corp"]`, or `ldap.open = ["127.0.0.1"]` plus `net.internal`. Every dial ends in `LdapError` kind `Unavailable`; the benches measure the refusal of a name or host the grant does not hold. The `.nvst` cases that reach Samba write their own `[ldap.corp]` beside them.

**The rest of Stage 10 splits in two.** The value classes (`Filter`, `Dn`, `Sid`, `Ad`, `Change`, and maybe `Ad\AccountFlags` and `Ad\GroupType`) can be built without a server, so their examples run as any other `Core` example does. `Connection`, `Entries`, `Entry` and `Changes` need a live connection, and no example can get one at a closed port: that needs a decision (see Backlog) before their proofs are written.

Server cases reach `samba-ad` (`tests/db/compose.yaml`) at `ldaps://localhost:16636`, plain LDAP at 16389. Write cases use OU and user names no other case uses; grep `tests/conformance/core/ldap-*.nvst` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs` before taking one.

next.title: the feature proofs, the value classes

items.text: **`Core\Ldap\Filter`'s members owe nothing** (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`): `about.md`, three examples, one attack and one bench each, a `covers:` marker on a Rust test. Registry rows at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:1560`. No server: a filter is a value, so `toString()` prints what was built. `bun nv proofs --id 'Core\Ldap\Filter::parse'` lists what one member owes; every comment and `about.md` follows `AGENTS.md` § *Text an end user reads*, checked with `bun nv proofs --comments`, and `bun nv proofs --record-perf --group 'Core\Ldap\Filter'` records the figures.
**`Core\Ldap\Dn`'s members owe nothing**, the same proofs, registry rows at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:1882`.

**`Core\Ldap\Sid`, `Core\Ldap\Ad` and `Core\Ldap\Change` owe nothing**, if the first two leave room: rows at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:2060`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:2186` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:967`.

backlog: **Decide how `Connection`, `Entries`, `Entry` and `Changes` examples get a live connection** (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`, `docs/examples/README.md` § *A grant the examples need*): an example must run with no network, so the choices are a `// requires:` marker in `tools/nv/proofs/run.ts:69` that runs it against `samba-ad` when the container is up, or a scripted loopback peer like the one `a_write_to_a_global_catalog_block_throws_before_it_is_sent` uses. Prefer the marker; it keeps the example a program a reader copies.

`Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` and `Ad\GroupType`: check whether `with` builds one without an `Entry`, which decides which half of Stage 10 they are in (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:2346`, `:2642`).
A CA a program supplies to `Ldap::open` (Stage 4), and the schema wired into the readers (Stage 6) — the goal's prose owns both.
